_meta.indication: ROZLYTREK is indicated for adult patients with metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC, and for adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with solid tumors that have an NTRK gene fusion (without a known acquired resistance mutation) that are metastatic or where surgical resection is likely to result in severe morbidity and have progressed following treatment or have no satisfactory alternative therapy.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Pooled ROS1-positive NSCLC subgroup from ALKA, STARTRK-1, and STARTRK-2
pivotal_trials.phase: Dose-finding and activity-estimating trials (Phase 1/2 basket program)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, single-arm, open-label trials; ORR and DOR by blinded independent central review per RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with recurrent or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC, ECOG PS ≤2, no prior ROS1 inhibitor
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) by BICR per RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.n: Efficacy assessed in 51 patients with ROS1-positive NSCLC
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 78% (95% CI 65, 89); CR 6%, PR 73%; DOR ≥12 months in 55% and ≥18 months in 30% of responders

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Pooled NTRK gene fusion-positive solid tumor subgroup from ALKA, STARTRK-1, and STARTRK-2
pivotal_trials.phase: Dose-finding and activity-estimating trials (Phase 1/2 basket program)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, single-arm, open-label trials; ORR and DOR by BICR per RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic solid tumors harboring an NTRK gene fusion who progressed following systemic therapy or would require morbid surgery; no prior TRK inhibitor
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) by BICR per RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.n: Efficacy assessed in the first 54 adult patients with NTRK gene fusion solid tumors
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 57% (95% CI 43, 71); CR 7.4%, PR 50%; DOR ≥6 months in 68% and ≥12 months in 45% of responders

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were fatigue, constipation, dysgeusia, edema, dizziness, diarrhea, nausea, dysesthesia, dyspnea, myalgia, cognitive impairment, increased weight, cough, vomiting, pyrexia, arthralgia, and vision disorders. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 39% of patients; most frequent (≥2%) were pneumonia (3.9%), dyspnea (3.7%), and pleural effusion (3.4%). Permanent discontinuation due to an adverse reaction occurred in 9% of patients.
target_moa: Entrectinib is an inhibitor of the TRK kinases (TRKA/B/C, encoded by NTRK1/2/3), ROS1, and ALK with IC50 values of 0.1 to 2 nM; fusion proteins involving TRK, ROS1 or ALK drive tumorigenesis through hyperactivation of downstream signaling.
companion_dx_detail: No FDA-approved companion diagnostic was available at approval for either indication; the sponsor agreed to a postmarketing commitment to develop and seek approval of a companion diagnostic (F1CDx) for NTRK-fusion solid tumors.

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this NDA to an advisory committee because no review issues were identified that raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Tumor response rate (ORR) and durability of response; for the NTRK-fusion solid tumor indication, ORR may be considered a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response [see *Clinical Studies* (14.2)].
ORR may be considered a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit when the treatment effect is large and the responses are durable.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Two accelerated-approval postmarketing requirements (3689-1 and 3689-2) to verify and describe clinical benefit in NTRK-fusion solid tumors through the final report of the first 54 patients and ongoing/proposed trials with more precise ORR and mature response duration.

citations.quote: We remind you of your two accelerated approval postmarketing requirements specified in your submission dated August 8, 2019.

3689-1 Submit the final report, including datasets, from the first 54 patients with NTRK-fusion solid tumors enrolled across the ALKA, STARTRK-1 [NCT02097810], and STARTRK-2 [NCT02568267] studies to verify and describe the clinical benefit and further characterize the duration of response in patients who achieved a complete or partial response to entrectinib.

basis.text: On May 12, 2017, entrectinib received breakthrough therapy designation for unresectable or metastatic solid tumors with NTRK-fusion proteins in adults who require systemic therapy and who progressed following prior treatment or have no acceptable alternative treatments.

citations.quote: On May 12, 2017, entrectinib received breakthrough therapy designation for the treatment of unresectable or metastatic solid tumors with *NTRK*-fusion proteins in adult patients who require systemic therapy and who have either progressed following prior treatment or who have no acceptable alternative treatments.

orphan_indication.text: On February 3, 2015, entrectinib received orphan drug designation for treatment of TrkA-positive, TrkB-positive, TrkC-positive, ROS1-positive or ALK-positive NSCLC.

citations.quote: February 3, 2015	Entrectinib received orphan drug designation for treatment of TrkA-positive, TrkB-positive, TrkC-positive, ROS1-positive or ALK-positive NSCLC under IND 120500.

basis.text: The application received priority review; breakthrough therapy designation resulted in priority review of this application.

citations.quote: Breakthrough therapy designation conferred to entrectinib resulted in increased and enhanced interactions with an experienced multidisciplinary review team including upper level management, in addition to priority review of this application.

summary.text: This priority-review NDA received December 18, 2018 was granted breakthrough therapy designation (May 12, 2017) and orphan drug designation (February 3, 2015). The NTRK gene fusion solid tumor indication was granted accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response, with two postmarketing requirements to verify clinical benefit.

requirement.text: 3689-1: Submit the final report and datasets from the first 54 patients with NTRK-fusion solid tumors enrolled across ALKA, STARTRK-1 (NCT02097810), and STARTRK-2 (NCT02568267) to verify and describe clinical benefit and characterize duration of response.

citations.quote: 3689-1 Submit the final report, including datasets, from the first 54 patients with NTRK-fusion solid tumors enrolled across the ALKA, STARTRK-1 [NCT02097810], and STARTRK-2 [NCT02568267] studies to verify and describe the clinical benefit and further characterize the duration of response in patients who achieved a complete or partial response to entrectinib.

requirement.text: 3689-2: Submit the final report from ongoing and proposed trials to verify clinical benefit through more precise estimation of ORR and mature response duration in adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with NTRK gene fusion solid tumors.

citations.quote: 3689-2 Submit the final report, including datasets, from ongoing and proposed trials conducted to verify and describe the clinical benefit of entrectinib, through more precise estimation of the overall response rate and mature response duration per independent review assessment, in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with solid tumors with a neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase (NTRK) gene fusion

requirement.text: 3689-3: Determine functional activation or inhibition of off-target receptors, transporters and/or channels showing >50% inhibition by entrectinib or M5 at 10 µM in secondary pharmacology studies.

citations.quote: 3689-3 Determine functional activation or inhibition of off-target receptors, transporters, and/or channels that, at concentrations of 10 \muM, showed greater than 50% inhibition by entrectinib or M5 in the secondary pharmacology studies submitted to NDA 212725 and 212726.

requirement.text: 3689-4: Submit integrated safety analyses and supporting data from clinical trial(s) designed to characterize cardiac risks and sequelae of entrectinib and support labeling instructions for dose modification and monitoring.

citations.quote: 3689-4 Submit integrated safety analyses and supporting data from an adequate number of patients enrolled in clinical trial(s) designed to characterize the cardiac risks and its sequelae in patients exposed to entrectinib with reasonable precision

requirement.text: 3689-5: Conduct clinical trial(s) in pediatric patients 12 years and older with NTRK-fusion solid tumors to evaluate potential long-term effects of entrectinib on growth and development, including neurological outcomes.

citations.quote: 3689-5 Conduct clinical trial(s) of entrectinib in a sufficient number of pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with NTRK-fusion solid tumors to evaluate the potential serious risk of adverse long-term effects of entrectinib on growth and development, including neurological outcomes with reasonable precision.

requirement.text: 3689-6: Submit integrated safety analyses and supporting data from clinical trial(s) designed to characterize the risk of fractures and sequelae of entrectinib and support labeling to mitigate the risk of skeletal fractures.

citations.quote: 3689-6 Submit integrated safety analyses and supporting data from an adequate number of patients enrolled in clinical trial(s) designed to characterize the risk of fractures and its sequelae in patients exposed to entrectinib with reasonable precision

requirement.text: 3689-7: Complete a pharmacokinetic trial to evaluate the effect of moderate and severe hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics and safety of entrectinib compared with subjects with normal hepatic function.

citations.quote: 3689-7 Complete a pharmacokinetic trial to evaluate the effect of moderate and severe hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics and safety of Rozlytrek (entrectinib) compared to subjects with normal hepatic function

requirement.text: 3689-8: Provide analytical and clinical validation results to support labeling of the F1CDx test to detect NTRK rearrangements for identifying patients who may benefit from entrectinib.
